questions.stem: In the given figure, the square and the triangle have same resistance per unit length. Find the ratio of their resistances about adjacent corners.
questions.solution:
Let the resistance per unit length be $\lambda$, then
For square,
$$R_{\text{Square}} = \frac{\left(\frac{3\lambda a}{4}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda a}{4}\right)}{\frac{3\lambda a}{4} + \frac{\lambda a}{4}} = \frac{3\lambda a}{16}$$
For triangle,
$$R_{\text{Triangle}} = \frac{\left(\frac{2\lambda a}{3}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda a}{3}\right)}{\frac{2\lambda a}{3} + \frac{\lambda a}{3}} = \frac{2\lambda a}{9}$$
$$\frac{R_{\text{Square}}}{R_{\text{Triangle}}} = \frac{3\lambda a}{16} \times \frac{a}{2\lambda a} = \frac{27}{32}$$

questions.stem: There is smooth ring of radius $R$ in vertical plane. A spring of natural length $R$ & elastic constant $K$ is vertical along a diameter. The free end is connected to bead of mass $m$ & when slightly disturbed it reaches point $C$ with speed $v$ where $v$ is
questions.solution:
Loss in PE = gain in KE
$$\frac{1}{2}K\left(R^{2}\right) - \frac{1}{2}K\left(\sqrt{2}-1\right)^{2}R^{2} + mgR = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}KR^{2}\left\{1 - 2 - 1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right\} + mgR = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$$
$$KR^{2}\left(\sqrt{2}-1\right) + mgR = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$$
$$\sqrt{\frac{2KR^{2}\left(\sqrt{2}-1\right) + 2mgR}{m}} = v$$

questions.stem: Surace mass density varies as $\sigma = \frac{\sigma_0 x}{ab}$ for the given plane sheet. Find the position of centre of mass for the distribution given
questions.solution:
As there is no variation of mass density in $y$ direction. So
$$y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{b}{2}.$$
Now for $x$ direction
$$dm = \left(\frac{\sigma_0 x}{ab}\right)b.dx$$
$$x_{cm} = \frac{\int_{0}^{a} x\,dm}{\int_{0}^{a} dm} = \frac{\frac{\sigma_0}{a}\int_{0}^{a} x^{2}dx}{\frac{\sigma_0}{a}\int xdx}$$
$$\Rightarrow x_{cm} = \frac{a^{3} \times 2}{3 \times a^{2}} = \frac{2}{3}a$$
So $r_{cm} = \frac{2}{3}a, \frac{b}{2}$

questions.stem: Energy of photon of wavelength $\lambda$ is $E_0$ which is equal to kinetic energy of proton of mass $m_p$. The ratio of de Broglie wavelengths of proton and photon is
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{2}m_p v^{2} = E_0 \Rightarrow p = \sqrt{2m_p E_0}$ $\quad \lambda_p = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_p E_0}}$
for photon $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = E_0 \Rightarrow \lambda_{ph} = \frac{hc}{E_0}$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_{ph}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_p E_0}} \times \frac{E_0}{hc} = \frac{1}{c}\sqrt{\frac{E_0}{2m_p}}$$

questions.stem: The lengths of a rectangular sheet is measured from a screw gauge of pitch $0.75\ \mathrm{mm}$ and number of division on circular scale = 15. Find maximum possible error in measurement of area.
questions.solution:
Lest count of screw gauge
$$= \frac{0.75}{15} = 0.05\ \mathrm{mm}$$
Now, $S = lb$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta S}{S} = \frac{\Delta l}{l} + \frac{\Delta b}{b}$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta S}{S} = \left(\frac{0.05}{5}\right) + \frac{0.05}{2.5} = \frac{1}{100} + \frac{2}{100} = \frac{3}{100}$$
$$\Delta S = \left(\frac{3}{100}\right) \times 5 \times 2.5 = 0.375\ \mathrm{mm^{2}}$$

questions.stem: The energy associated with a cylindrical region due to an EM wave $E = 100\sin(kx - \omega t)$ is $U_0$. Find the equation of EM wave for which a cylinder of same length and half the diameter (as previous one) contains same energy $U_0$.
questions.solution:
For EM wave $E = 100\sin(\omega t - kx)$
Energy density $\rho_{a_v} = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 (E_0)^{2}$
Initial volume $v_0 = \pi R^{2}l$
Volume in next situation = $v = \frac{\pi R^{2}l}{4} = \frac{V_0}{4}$
So, $u_0 = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 (E_0)^{2} \times V_0 = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 (E_1^{2}) \cdot \frac{V_0}{4}$
$$\Rightarrow E_0^{2} = \frac{E_1^{2}}{4} \Rightarrow E_1 = 2E_0 = 200\ \mathrm{V/m}$$
So, required equation will have 200 V/m of amplitude.

$$y_2 = \frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} \times y_1$$
